title: U.S. House · Connecticut's 5th District
area: Northwestern and north-central Connecticut, including Waterbury, Danbury, New Britain, and Torrington

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Jahana Hayes advanced without appearing on the ballot. Chris Shea defeated Jonathan De Barros in the Republican primary, winning 81% of the vote. The Cook Political Report rated this district D+3 based on 2024 presidential results, making it the most competitive of Connecticut's five U.S. House seats.

summary.text: Jahana Hayes is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. A former public-school teacher and 2016 National Teacher of the Year, she serves on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce committees.

background.text: Born in Waterbury, Connecticut, in 1973; earned an associate degree from Naugatuck Valley Community College, a bachelor's degree from Southern Connecticut State University, and graduate degrees from the University of Saint Joseph and the University of Bridgeport.
Worked as a public-school teacher before running for Congress.
Has represented Connecticut's 5th District in the U.S. House since 2019, currently serving her fourth term.

priorities.text: Says she has been a strong proponent of "commonsense gun laws that keeps our communities safe," supporting universal background checks, community violence prevention funding, and safe storage.

Says her work has centered on "reducing systemic barriers to healthcare that cause disparities, while increasing access and affordability," including lowering drug prices and stabilizing the Affordable Care Act.
Says she has introduced proposals to "mitigate carbon emissions and conserve our ecosystems, while creating high-wage, union jobs," and has been an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal.

positions.summary: Says she has supported legislation for universal background checks, community violence prevention funding, and safe storage, and serves as Deputy Whip on the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.
positions.quote: She has supported legislation for universal background checks, community violence prevention funding, and safe storage.

positions.summary: Says she supported legislation during the COVID-19 pandemic to expand insurance and provide emergency coverage to people who lost coverage, and has supported legislation to strengthen Medicare and Medicaid and lower drug prices.
positions.quote: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Congresswoman Hayes supported legislation that would expand insurance and provide emergency coverage to the millions of individuals who lost coverage.

positions.summary: Has introduced legislation to mitigate carbon emissions, secured billions in federal funding to replace diesel school buses with zero-emissions buses, and has been an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal since her first term.
positions.quote: Since her first term, she has been an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal and knows climate change mitigation must be centered in every policy Congress considers.

positions.summary: Says she has advocated for the expansion of protections for renters through the pandemic and supports the Build Back Better Act's investments in affordable housing and rental assistance.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Hayes has advocated for the expansion of protections for renters, landlords and homeowners though the pandemic.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 2025–2026 Congress.
Chaired the Agriculture Subcommittee on Nutrition, Oversight, and Department Operations in the 2021–2022 Congress.
Served as ranking member of the Agriculture Subcommittee on Nutrition, Foreign Agriculture, and Horticulture in the 2023–2024 Congress.
Introduced the Clean School Bus Act and Clean Commute for Kids Act and negotiated $5 billion for these proposals in the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.
